question: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Third Amendment) Bill, 2022, seeks to amend the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, with respect to its application to _____________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Third Amendment) Bill, 2022, seeks to amend the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, specifically for **Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• This amendment aims to include new communities under the category of **Scheduled Tribes** in Himachal Pradesh.
 
• The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, originally identified communities that qualify as Scheduled Tribes in different states and union territories of India.
 
• The inclusion or exclusion of communities under Scheduled Tribes is critical for ensuring access to **reserved benefits** such as educational quotas, job opportunities, and welfare schemes.
 
• The amendment reflects the government’s attempt to address the socio-economic and cultural needs of tribal communities in Himachal Pradesh by legally recognizing them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scheduled Tribes in India:**

 
 
• Scheduled Tribes are officially designated groups of people in India recognized as socially and economically disadvantaged.
 
• They are listed under Article 342 of the Indian Constitution, which gives the President the authority to specify Scheduled Tribes in consultation with the Governor of a state.
 
• India is home to over **705 Scheduled Tribes**, as per the 2011 Census.
 
• Benefits provided to Scheduled Tribes include reservation in education, employment, and legislative bodies, as well as specific welfare schemes.
 
 
 
• **Himachal Pradesh and Tribal Communities:**
 
 
• Himachal Pradesh is known for its diverse tribal population, including groups such as **Gaddis, Kinnauras, Gujjars, Pangwal, and Lahaulas**.
 
• Tribal communities in Himachal Pradesh primarily reside in remote areas, including **Lahaul-Spiti, Kinnaur, and Pangi**.
 
• These communities depend on agriculture, animal husbandry, and handicrafts for their livelihood.
 
• Efforts to include new communities aim to address the socio-economic challenges faced by these groups.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions for Scheduled Tribes:**
 
 
• Article 342 allows the President to declare tribes or tribal communities as Scheduled Tribes.
 
• Article 15 and Article 16 provide **reservation in education and employment** for Scheduled Tribes.
 
• Article 330 and Article 332 ensure **representation in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies**.
 
• Article 46 directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of Scheduled Tribes.
 
 
 
• **Amendment Process for Scheduled Tribes List:**
 
 
• The inclusion or exclusion of communities in the Scheduled Tribes list requires legislative approval through a constitutional amendment.
 
• The process involves consultation with the concerned state government and validation by the Parliament.
 
• Such amendments are critical for ensuring that identified tribes benefit from government schemes and legal protections.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, was enacted to identify tribal communities across India.
 
• Several amendments have been introduced over the years to update the list of Scheduled Tribes based on evolving socio-political and cultural needs.
 
• These changes reflect the Indian government’s commitment to recognizing and addressing the challenges faced by indigenous communities.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Welfare Programs:**
 
 
• Programs such as the **Vanbandhu Kalyan Yojana** and Tribal Sub-Plan aim to improve the living standards of tribal communities.
 
• Special focus is given to education, healthcare, and employment under these schemes.
 
• Institutions like the **National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST)** oversee the implementation of these welfare initiatives.
